content: {"summary":"The evidence shows that checkout latency spikes correspond to DNS lookup timeouts inside the orders‑api pod, not to slow database queries. Edge logs indicate the total request time is spent in orders‑api, DNS lookups are usually fast but occasionally exceed 5 s due to lost UDP replies, and the resolver configuration causes multiple queries per lookup, leading to 5 s retries that match the observed p99 latency.","likely_cause":"DNS resolver timeouts (lost UDP replies and retry delays) causing 5‑second pauses in the orders‑api pod","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"The request time is spent inside orders‑api, not downstream services","evidence_ids":["RB-021#2"],"quote":"The time is spent inside orders-api."},{"text":"Two DNS lookups took just over 5 seconds, matching the latency spikes","evidence_ids":["RB-021#3"],"quote":"Two took just over 5,000 ms."},{"text":"A single lookup generates eight UDP queries, so a lost reply triggers a 5‑second timeout","evidence_ids":["RB-021#4"],"quote":"One lookup is 4 names × 2 record types = 8 queries over UDP."},{"text":"Most lookups complete in 1‑3 ms, indicating the database queries themselves are fast","evidence_ids":["RB-021#3"],"quote":"Most took 1 to 3 ms."}],"next_checks":["Capture DNS query/response logs from the pod to confirm lost UDP replies","Run a trace of getaddrinfo calls to see retry behavior","Measure raw PostgreSQL query latency from inside the pod to verify it remains sub‑millisecond","Disable the search suffixes in /etc/resolv.conf temporarily and repeat the checkout load test","Increase libuv thread‑pool size and observe impact on latency spikes"]}
